title: Induction and sums
description: Questions on strong induction, sums of powers, areas and volumes from sums, and which endless sums settle.

questions.question: In strong induction, what may you assume when proving $$P(k + 1)$$?
questions.explanation: That is the strong inductive step (:ref{#strong-induction}), used for factorising into primes.

questions.question: Which number is prime?
questions.explanation: $$29$$ has no divisors but $$1$$ and itself; $$27 = 3^3$$, $$51 = 3 \cdot 17$$, and $$1$$ isn't prime by definition (:ref{#prime}).

questions.question: Why do the 4p and 5p stamp proofs need four base cases (12p to 15p)?
options: Each amount is built by swapping a 4p stamp for a 5p stamp in the amount one less
Each amount is built by adding a 4p stamp to the amount four less
questions.explanation: The step goes from $$n - 4$$ to $$n$$, so four starting amounts are needed (:ref{#stamps}).

questions.question: What does Bernoulli's inequality say about $$1.01^{100}$$?
questions.explanation: $$(1 + h)^n \ge 1 + nh = 1 + 100 \cdot 0.01$$ (:ref{#bernoulli}).

questions.question: How many mappings are there from a set of $$5$$ elements to a set of $$2$$?
questions.explanation: Each of the $$5$$ elements has $$2$$ choices: $$2^5$$ (:ref{#counting-mappings}).

questions.question: What is $$1 + 2 + \cdots + 10$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{10 \cdot 11}{2}$$ (:ref{#sum-integers}).

questions.question: How many oranges are in a square pyramid $$10$$ layers high?
questions.explanation: $$1^2 + \cdots + 10^2 = \frac{10 \cdot 11 \cdot 21}{6}$$ (:ref{#sum-squares}).

questions.question: What is $$1 + 3 + 5 + \cdots + 13$$?
questions.explanation: The first $$7$$ odd numbers add to $$7^2$$ (:ref{#sum-odd}).

questions.question: What is $$1^3 + 2^3 + \cdots + 5^3$$?
questions.explanation: The sum of the first $$n$$ cubes is $$(1 + \cdots + n)^2 = 15^2$$ (:ref{#sum-cubes}).

questions.question: What is $$\frac{1}{1 \cdot 2} + \frac{1}{2 \cdot 3} + \cdots + \frac{1}{9 \cdot 10}$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{1}{k(k + 1)} = \frac1k - \frac{1}{k + 1}$$, and the sum telescopes to $$1 - \frac{1}{10}$$ (:ref{#telescoping}).

questions.question: What is the area under $$y = x^2$$ from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1$$?
questions.explanation: Inner and outer strips squeeze it to exactly $$\frac13$$ (:ref{#parabola-area}).

questions.question: Why does $$\lvert A - \frac13 \rvert \le \frac1n$$ for every $$n$$ prove $$A = \frac13$$?
options: It doesn't, it only gets close
Any gap would be bigger than $$\frac1n$$ for some $$n$$
Because the strips end up with width $$0$$
questions.explanation: If $$A \ne \frac13$$, pick $$n$$ larger than $$\frac{1}{\lvert A - 1/3 \rvert}$$ for a contradiction (:ref{#areas-and-volumes-squeeze}).

questions.question: What is the volume of a cone with base radius $$r$$ and height $$h$$?
questions.explanation: A third of the cylinder around it (:ref{#cone-volume}).

questions.question: What is the volume of a ball of radius $$r$$?
questions.explanation: Found by slicing a half ball into cylinders (:ref{#ball-volume}).

questions.question: What is $$1 + \frac13 + \frac19 + \cdots$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{1}{1 - c}$$ with $$c = \frac13$$ (:ref{#geometric-series}).

questions.question: What does $$1 - \frac12 + \frac14 - \frac18 + \cdots$$ settle towards?
questions.explanation: $$c = -\frac12$$, so the sum is $$\frac{1}{1 + 1/2}$$ (:ref{#geometric-series}).

questions.question: Which fraction is $$0.363636\ldots$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{36}{99} = \frac{4}{11}$$ (:ref{#repeating-decimals}).

questions.question: What does it mean that $$s_n$$ settles towards $$L$$?
options: For every margin, from some point on every $$s_n$$ is within it of $$L$$
questions.explanation: That is the definition (:ref{#settles-towards}); "infinity" is not a number.

questions.question: Does $$1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \cdots$$ settle?
options: No: the sums grow without bound
questions.explanation: The formula $$\frac{1}{1 - c}$$ needs $$\lvert c \rvert < 1$$ (:ref{#geometric-series}).

questions.question: Does $$1 + \frac12 + \frac13 + \frac14 + \cdots$$ settle?
options: Yes, because the terms shrink to $$0$$
No: it grows past every number, slowly
questions.explanation: Grouping shows the sum up to $$\frac{1}{2^m}$$ is at least $$1 + \frac m2$$ (:ref{#harmonic-unbounded}). Shrinking terms aren't enough.

questions.question: What can you say about $$1 + \frac14 + \frac19 + \cdots + \frac{1}{n^2}$$?
questions.explanation: Comparing with $$\frac{1}{(k - 1)k}$$ and telescoping gives at most $$2 - \frac1n$$ (:ref{#reciprocal-squares-bounded}).

questions.question: Why do the reciprocal squares settle towards a number?
options: The sums only grow and stay below $$2$$
Each term is smaller than the one before
questions.explanation: Increasing sums with an upper bound settle, taken as given (:ref{#bounded-increasing}).

questions.question: An induction step only works from $$k \ge 4$$. What must you check?
options: $$P(4)$$ as the base case; the step then carries it to every $$n \ge 4$$
questions.explanation: Induction can start at any number (:ref{#basic-proofs/induction}); the base case must be where the step begins to work. Cases below $$4$$ must be checked by hand if you want them.

questions.question: A "proof" that all crayons in a box share a colour breaks where?
options: Going from $$1$$ crayon to $$2$$: the two groups don't overlap
questions.explanation: The step needs a crayon in both groups, which fails when $$k = 1$$.

questions.question: Which is $$360$$ as a product of primes?
questions.explanation: $$8 \cdot 9 \cdot 5 = 360$$, with only primes (:ref{#prime-factorisation}).

questions.question: What is $$1 \cdot 2 + 2 \cdot 3 + 3 \cdot 4$$?
questions.explanation: $$2 + 6 + 12$$; in general it is $$\frac{n(n + 1)(n + 2)}{3}$$, from the sums of squares and numbers (:ref{#sum-squares}).

questions.question: Is $$(1 + 2 + \cdots + n)^2$$ equal to $$1^2 + 2^2 + \cdots + n^2$$?
questions.explanation: At $$n = 2$$: $$9$$ against $$5$$. The square of the sum is the sum of cubes (:ref{#sum-cubes}).

questions.question: Under $$y = x^2$$ on $$[0, 1]$$ with $$n$$ strips, how far apart are the inner and outer totals?
questions.explanation: The difference is the tallest outer rectangle, $$1 \cdot \frac1n$$ (:ref{#areas-and-volumes-strip-sums}).

questions.question: What is the area under $$y = x^2$$ from $$0$$ to $$3$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{b^3}{3}$$ with $$b = 3$$ (:ref{#areas-and-volumes-parabola-to-b}).

questions.question: Which fact about volume is taken as given in the slicing arguments?
options: A cylinder's volume is its base area times its height
questions.explanation: Cylinders are the slices, and their volume is taken as given (:ref{#areas-and-volumes-cylinder}).

questions.question: A dose $$D$$ is taken daily and a fraction $$f < 1$$ remains each day. What does the amount settle towards?
questions.explanation: The amount is $$D(1 + f + f^2 + \cdots)$$, a geometric series (:ref{#geometric-series}).

questions.question: What is $$1 + \frac34 + \left(\frac34\right)^2 + \cdots$$?
questions.explanation: $$\frac{1}{1 - 3/4}$$ (:ref{#geometric-series}).

questions.question: Why do the powers $$c^n$$ shrink to $$0$$ when $$0 < c < 1$$?
options: Write $$\frac1c = 1 + h$$; Bernoulli makes $$\frac{1}{c^n} \ge 1 + nh$$ grow
Each power is smaller than the one before, and that is enough
questions.explanation: So $$c^n \le \frac{1}{1 + nh}$$, which gets as small as you like (:ref{#powers-shrink}, :ref{#bernoulli}).

questions.question: What is $$1 + \frac12 + \frac13 + \frac14$$?
questions.explanation: Over the common denominator $$12$$: $$\frac{12 + 6 + 4 + 3}{12}$$. These partial sums grow without bound (:ref{#harmonic-unbounded}).

questions.question: What goes wrong with $$1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + \cdots$$?
options: The partial sums jump between $$1$$ and $$0$$, so it doesn't settle
questions.explanation: Grouping it two ways gives $$0$$ or $$1$$; a series that doesn't settle has no sum (:ref{#series}).
